```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, ggplot2, readr
library(skimr)
library(GGally)
library(caret)
library(randomForest)
set.seed(42)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))
```

## 1. Goal

Predict individual medical insurance **expenses** from demographic and health attributes, and identify which factors drive cost. Models compared: multiple linear regression, a Box-Cox / log-transformed regression with an interaction, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting.

## 2. Load and inspect the data

```{r load}
ins <- read_csv("data/medical_insurance.csv")
glimpse(ins)
skim(ins)
```

## 3. Cleaning

Three issues need handling:

* `premium` is derived from `expenses` (a small percentage of it). Using it as a predictor would leak the target, so it is dropped.
* `discount_eligibility` behaves like a smoker flag in this data (a small group with far higher expenses), so treat it as a *proxy* for smoking, not as a separate factor.
* Duplicate rows and factor types.

```{r clean}
cor(ins$expenses, ins$premium)          # shows the leakage

ins <- ins %>%
  distinct() %>%
  dplyr::select(-premium) %>%
  mutate(
    gender = factor(gender),
    discount_eligibility = factor(discount_eligibility, levels = c("no", "yes")),
    region = factor(region)
  )

cat("Rows after cleaning:", nrow(ins), "\n")
colSums(is.na(ins))
```

## 4. Exploratory data analysis

### Distribution of the target

```{r eda-target}
p1 <- ggplot(ins, aes(expenses)) + geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#6a5af0", colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Expenses are right-skewed", x = "Expenses")
p2 <- ggplot(ins, aes(log(expenses))) + geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#00b8a9", colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Log expenses are closer to normal", x = "log(Expenses)")
gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```

### Categorical drivers

```{r eda-cat}
ins %>%
  pivot_longer(c(gender, discount_eligibility, region), names_to = "var", values_to = "level") %>%
  ggplot(aes(level, expenses, fill = level)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~var, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "C", end = .85) +
  labs(title = "Expenses by category", x = NULL)
```

### Numeric drivers

```{r eda-num}
ggplot(ins, aes(bmi, expenses, colour = discount_eligibility)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .6) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(no = "#6a5af0", yes = "#ff5a36")) +
  labs(title = "BMI vs expenses, split by discount eligibility (smoker proxy)")

ggplot(ins, aes(age, expenses, colour = discount_eligibility)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(no = "#6a5af0", yes = "#ff5a36")) +
  labs(title = "Age vs expenses")

ggpairs(ins, columns = c("age", "bmi", "children", "expenses"))
```

## 5. Train / test split

```{r split}
idx   <- createDataPartition(ins$expenses, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train <- ins[idx, ]
test  <- ins[-idx, ]
c(train = nrow(train), test = nrow(test))

metrics <- function(actual, pred, model) {
  tibble(Model = model,
         RMSE = sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2)),
         MAE  = mean(abs(actual - pred)),
         R2   = cor(actual, pred)^2)
}
```

## 6. Model 1: multiple linear regression

```{r lm1}
m1 <- lm(expenses ~ ., data = train)
summary(m1)
```

### Diagnostics

```{r lm1-diag, fig.height=7}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2)); plot(m1); par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
car::vif(m1)
```

Check the residual plots: a funnel shape or curved trend means the linear model on raw expenses is mis-specified.

## 7. Model 2: Box-Cox transformation and interaction

```{r boxcox}
bc <- MASS::boxcox(m1, lambda = seq(-1, 1, 0.05))
lambda <- bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
lambda
```

A lambda near 0 supports a log transform of expenses. The scatter plot above also shows the BMI effect is much steeper for the smoker-proxy group, so add an interaction.

```{r lm2}
m2 <- lm(log(expenses) ~ age + bmi * discount_eligibility + children + gender + region, data = train)
summary(m2)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2)); plot(m2); par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Add an obesity threshold effect (BMI of 30 or more) as a further variant:

```{r lm3}
train <- train %>% mutate(obese = factor(bmi >= 30))
test  <- test  %>% mutate(obese = factor(bmi >= 30))
m3 <- lm(log(expenses) ~ age + bmi + obese * discount_eligibility + children + gender + region, data = train)
summary(m3)
AIC(m2, m3)   # lower is better (the models are not nested, so anova() would be invalid)
```

## 8. Models 3 and 4: Random Forest and Gradient Boosting

```{r ml}
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)
f <- expenses ~ age + bmi + children + gender + discount_eligibility + region

rf <- train(f, data = train, method = "rf", trControl = ctrl, ntree = 300,
            tuneGrid = expand.grid(mtry = c(2, 4, 6, 8)), importance = TRUE)

gbm_fit <- train(f, data = train, method = "gbm", trControl = ctrl, verbose = FALSE,
                 tuneGrid = expand.grid(n.trees = c(100, 300, 500),
                                        interaction.depth = c(1, 2, 3),
                                        shrinkage = 0.05, n.minobsinnode = 10))
rf$bestTune
gbm_fit$bestTune
```

## 9. Compare models on the held-out test set

```{r compare}
pred <- tibble(
  actual = test$expenses,
  lm_raw = predict(m1, test),
  lm_log_interaction = exp(predict(m2, test)),
  lm_log_obese = exp(predict(m3, test)),
  rf = predict(rf, test),
  gbm = predict(gbm_fit, test)
)

results <- bind_rows(
  metrics(pred$actual, pred$lm_raw, "Linear (raw)"),
  metrics(pred$actual, pred$lm_log_interaction, "Log-linear + BMI x smoker-proxy"),
  metrics(pred$actual, pred$lm_log_obese, "Log-linear + obese x smoker-proxy"),
  metrics(pred$actual, pred$rf, "Random Forest"),
  metrics(pred$actual, pred$gbm, "Gradient Boosting")
) %>% arrange(RMSE)

knitr::kable(results, digits = 3)
```

Back-transforming log predictions with `exp()` slightly underestimates the mean; a smearing correction would reduce that bias but is skipped here for simplicity.

```{r pred-plot}
pred %>%
  pivot_longer(-actual, names_to = "model", values_to = "predicted") %>%
  ggplot(aes(actual, predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .4, colour = "#6a5af0") +
  geom_abline(colour = "#ff5a36", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  labs(title = "Predicted vs actual expenses (test set)")
```

## 10. What drives cost?

```{r importance}
plot(varImp(rf), main = "Random Forest variable importance")
plot(varImp(gbm_fit), main = "Gradient Boosting variable importance")
```
